rows.grounds: absolutive gerund expressing prior or concurrent pervasion
demonstrative used to draw consequence from prior analogy
noun qualified by brahma and mahat

items.question: What justifies the claim that the great Brahman-state pervades and abides everywhere?
premises: The preceding analogy illustrates pervasion without division.
What pervades all limited forms remains present in them.
Brahman is identified as that all-pervading reality.
items.inference: Therefore the great state of Brahman stands everywhere by pervading all.
items.plain_english: Having pervaded all, the great state of Brahman therefore stands everywhere.
